title: Operator quick hypothesis catalog and observability checklist
content:
Purpose and intent:
This is a lightweight, operator-focused hypothesis catalog + quick checklist for time-boxed investigations during incidents or P1s. The goal is to give on-call and triage engineers a short, searchable set of likely causes, the minimum correlated signals to check, and dashboard widgets/trace anchors to open in parallel.

Notes on usage:
- Keep this doc open during the first 10 minutes of an incident.
- Run the quick checks in parallel (A/B teams) rather than serially.
- Add new hypotheses here as we learn from postmortems.
- Not exhaustive; this prioritizes our token-serving inference topology (router -> model pool -> KV cache -> storage).

Quick top-of-page checklist (10m triage):
1) Is system-wide SLO/alert firing? Check global SLO panel (error rate, p99 latency).
2) Scope: tenant-specific or global? Pull tenant_id from sample traces or request logs.
3) Resource constraints: GPU utilization, host OOMs, scheduler queue length.
4) Cache coldness: per-tenant cache hit rate drop.
5) Model fallback: routing to slower variant or CPU fallback.
6) Network blips: increased retransmits to storage or model hosts.
7) Config changes/deploys in last 30m: check releases + config-rollout dashboard.

Hypothesis catalog (fast checks + key signals):
- H1: Sudden multi-tenant latency spike due to cache churn
  - Quick checks: per-tenant kv_cache_hit_rate, cache_eviction_rate, cache-warmth index; p50/p95 of kv_access latency.
  - Trace anchors: span tags kv_hit=true/false, kv_lookup_ms, cache_key_family.
  - Dashboard widgets: time series of kv_hit_rate (tenant), heatmap of cache key churn, per-model cold-start rate.
  - If true: warm popular prefixes, bump cache size, enable short-term cache pin for top tenants.

- H2: Autoscaler misconfiguration causing queueing/backpressure
  - Quick checks: scheduler_queue_length, pod_start_latency, provisioner_backlog, scale_events timeline.
  - Trace anchors: request_enqueue_span, scheduling_decision_span, node_assignment_tag.
  - Dashboard widgets: stacked area of queued requests by model, recent scale events table.
  - If true: rollback autoscaler config, emergency manual scale, add safe fallback policy.

- H3: Model variant fallback (slower CPU or quantized path) triggered by capacity shortfall
  - Quick checks: routing_policy_events, model_variant_ratio, per-request model_name seen in traces.
  - Trace anchors: model_load/variant_span, model_exec_path, hardware_tag (GPU/CPU).
  - Dashboard widgets: per-route model variant breakdown, latency by variant.
  - If true: route to higher-capacity pool or enable degraded but faster variant; notify product if quality impact is acceptable.

- H4: Downstream storage latency (embedding store / KV backing)
  - Quick checks: storage_p50/p95/p99, retry_rate, storage_error_rate, connection_pool_exhaustion.
  - Trace anchors: store_rpc_span with backend host, db_conn_pool_size.
  - Dashboard widgets: callout panel for storage latency across regions, speculative retry counters.
  - If true: fail open to cached copy, throttle writes, increase DB capacity.

- H5: Sudden tenant-specific throttling due to quota enforcement bug
  - Quick checks: rate_limit_rejections, quota_evaluator_errors, api_key_lookup_errors.
  - Trace anchors: quota_check_span, throttle_reason tag.
  - Dashboard widgets: per-tenant rejection counter, recent config change audit.
  - If true: emergency mute quota enforcer for affected tenant(s), open follow-up bug.

Minimum telemetry to capture in traces (span-level attributes we care about):
- request_id
- tenant_id (hashed)
- route_name / api_path
- model_name + model_version
- model_variant (quantized / fp16 / cpu)
- hardware (gpu_type / cpu)
- sequence_length_estimate / prompt_token_count
- kv_cache_hit (boolean)
- kv_lookup_ms
- enqueue_ms / dequeue_ms
- total_tokens_generated
- rollout_tag / canary_id
- priority (normal/low/high)
- error_code / internal_error_type

Sampling guidance for traces (practical):
- Always sample 100% of requests with errors and requests that hit > p95 latency.
- Rate-limit sampling of successful requests: 1% global baseline, 5% for tenants > X qps and all requests from paid-tier.
- Synthetic/canary traffic: 100% sampling and a dedicated tag so they can be filtered.
- When a P1 occurs, flip a temporary high-sampling rule for the affected route/tenant for 30–60 minutes.

Metric definitions (short canonical forms):
- infra.scheduler_queue_length: instantaneous queue length for requests waiting to be scheduled. Unit: count. Owner: infra-queue-svc. Alert: > 500 for > 5m.
- inference.kv_cache_hit_rate: fraction of KV cache lookups that succeeded (0..1). Unit: ratio. Owner: serving-runtime. Alert: drop > 15% from baseline for > 3m.
- inference.model_exec_p99_ms: 99th percentile model execution (inference forward) time excluding enqueue. Unit: ms. Owner: serving-runtime. Alert: p99 > 1200ms for > 5m.
- routing.model_variant_fallback_rate: fraction of requests routed to fallback variants. Unit: ratio. Owner: routing-team. Alert: > 10% sustained.
- storage.rpc_error_rate: fraction of storage RPCs returning errors. Unit: ratio. Owner: storage-infra. Alert: > 1% sustained or spike > 5x baseline.

Dashboard composition notes (what to open first):
1) Incident overview panel (single row): global SLO status, active alerts, p95 global latency, error rate, recent deploys.
2) Tenant split row: top 10 tenants by error/latency, tenant heatmap, tenant cache_warmth.
3) Serving topology row: queue length, backend throughput, GPU utilization, model variant split.
4) KV cache row: per-tenant hit rate, eviction rate, key churn heatmap.
5) Traces & session row: sample traces link, recent high-latency traces, trace-anchored span waterfall.
6) Recent config and rollout row: config-change events, canary IDs, rollout percentages.

Recommended dashboard widgets and SQL snippets (operators):
- Recent high-latency requests (p99):
  SELECT request_id, tenant_id, route_name, model_name, latency_ms, started_at
  FROM request_events
  WHERE started_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '15 minutes' AND latency_ms > 800
  ORDER BY latency_ms DESC
- Top cache-miss keys (approx):
  SELECT cache_key_family, count(*) as misses
  FROM kv_access_log
  WHERE hit = false AND ts > NOW() - INTERVAL '1 hour'
  GROUP BY cache_key_family
  ORDER BY misses DESC
  LIMIT 50

Investigation playbook (first 30 min):
- 0-5m: run quick checklist, scope (tenant/global), mute noisy alerts where safe.
- 5-15m: open traces for 5 highest-latency requests, look for cross-service waits or retries.
- 15-30m: verify resource usage, check autoscaler events and recent deploys; enact mitigation (scale, warm caches, mute enforcer).
- 30-60m: postmortem seed: capture all hypotheses tested, actions taken, revert if required, schedule follow-ups.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Define a canonical per-tenant cache_warmth metric — current proxies emit different estimators (todo: unify).
- Add pre-built dashboard panel that links directly to 5 highest-latency traces for the selected tenant.
- Evaluate adding soft-fail gating on quota enforcer to reduce false-positive throttles.

Notes from ops run (recent learnings):
- A previous incident showed the importance of pairing the cache_hot_keys view with a short lived 'pin' (60s) which immediately reduced p99 latency for top tenants. Implemented as an ops cheat in the serving console.
- Autoscaler events can look benign if you only check CPU/GPU; you must inspect 'pod start failure' sub-events for image pull or init-container timeouts.

Appendix: useful links and queries
- Trace playbook (Confluence): confluence://OBS-trace-playbook
- Query collection repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/tree/main/queries/incident
- Quick dash: dashboards/ops-incident-quickview (Grafana)

If you add a hypothesis or update a threshold, append a short note here with date and rationale so we can iterate the catalog.
